routines.semantics: raw.cmprss(delim,n,input,lenout?) limits each consecutive run of the given ASCII delimiter to at most n bytes. Nonpositive n removes delimiter bytes. The default capacity fits the entire result. Explicit capacity includes NUL and can truncate on the right. Minimum capacity is 1, so capacity 1 on a valid call yields empty text. NUL delimiter is a legal by-value byte. Text is well-formed UTF-8 without embedded NUL. Encoded input and terminator fit signed32. WASM caps each buffer at 256 MiB.

scenarios.observes: Compare full output for short/long, separated and boundary runs under several retained-count limits.
Use space and control whitespace as distinct single-byte delimiters and retain all other whitespace exactly.
Observe empty input, exhausted delimiter-only input and unchanged absent-delimiter input.
Compare exact UTF-8 text including initial BOM, multibyte characters and trailing whitespace.
Truncate the compressed stream to the available bytes plus terminator, observing where runs occur relative to the truncation.
Use capacities terminating on complete multibyte boundaries and preserve every resulting character.
Compare actual STRINGTOOSHORT for zero output capacity and require subsequent recovery.
Pass a negative signed32 capacity to actual CSPICE with valid sentinel storage and compare STRINGTOOSHORT.
Pass NUL as a scalar delimiter. Complete non-NUL text and its spaces remain observable.
Use a very large valid signed32 capacity on a bounded input and observe the complete output using sufficient actual storage.

routines.edgeAssessment: Run lengths, nonpositive and signed32 counts, absent/NUL delimiters, empty/all-delimiter text and whitespace delimiters expose compression order. Buffer capacities from terminator-only through exact UTF-8 boundaries, BOM and MAX_INT distinguish truncation from trimming.
routines.errorAssessment: Actual below-minimum signed32 capacities signal STRINGTOOSHORT. Independent focused checks compare genuine errors, reset and a successful subsequent call. A capacity ending inside a UTF-8 scalar is a successful C call followed by a typed output-representation error. Malformed/non-string text, embedded NUL, unpaired surrogates, invalid integer arguments where applicable and unsafe buffers are separate wrapper guards.

findings.summary: The locked convenience conversion ignores invalid UTF-8 prefixes and strips trailing whitespace after the correct canonical symbol returns.

Independent byte probes compare the raw bytes and the convenience conversion.
